articles.title_orig: China Competetive Salary Guide: How to Win High-Skilled Talent
articles.title_zh: China Competetive Salary Guide: How to Win High-Skilled Talent
articles.content_orig:
Recruiting high-skilled and in-demand talent in China requires pay offers benchmarked by city, sector, and role, with statutory contributions and the 13th-month bonus built into the budget from the start. This China competitive salary guide sets out 2025 salary data by region, industry, and company type to help employers price offers that attract and retain talent.
For companies hiring high-skilled or in-demand talent in China, compensation strategy is one of the most consequential decisions to get right. These candidates operate in competitive segments of the labour market, where qualified talent can be scarce depending on industry and location, and where salary expectations, benchmarks, and negotiation norms differ considerably from the broader workforce.
Understanding current salary benchmarks, and how to apply them by region, sector, and role, is therefore essential both for setting a competitive offer and building a compensation strategy that helps attract and retain the skilled talent driving business growth in China.
While China doesn’t currently suffer from an economy-wide labour shortage, qualified talent pools can vary considerably depending on industry and location. Emerging fields, such as AI, renewables, semiconductors, biopharmaceuticals, and robotics, face nationwide shortages, as the educational pipeline catches up with market demand. However, some traditional industries also struggle to fill high-skilled positions, such as automation engineers or green manufacturing consultants in the manufacturing sector.
The rapid pace of change in the e-commerce industry has also led to a lack of qualified talent to fill tech- and compliance-related roles in particular, with demand driven by high levels of AI adoption and tightening anti-competition and data protection regulations within the sector.
China’s provincial governments publish annual catalogues of high-skilled talent in urgent demand, which provide a useful indicator of where there may be strong competition in recruitment.
Talent Shortages in Major Chinese Cities
Guangzhou (2025 catalogue)
Note: The above lists are only a sample of the in-demand job categories listed in the catalogues, not the full list.
In many specialised industries, talent can also be concentrated in a relatively small number of cities. China’s four tier-one cities – Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Guangzhou – along with a handful of fast-growing “new first tier” cities such as Hangzhou, Ningbo, Nanjing, Suzhou, Chengdu, and Chongqing, account for a disproportionate share of skilled candidates. This means location choice has an outsized effect on both the cost and the speed of hiring, with compensation packages potentially having to reflect relocation costs or incentives if companies are located away from the industrial hubs.
Foreign companies may also have additional language and soft skill requirements depending on how localised their operations are. Requirements for strong English or other foreign-language skills, overseas experience, or specific cultural fit will further narrow the pool of suitable candidates.
Due to the high level of competition, setting the right compensation level is central to attracting and keeping talent. Job seekers in China typically expect a salary increase when moving to a new role, and, while turnover rates have improved substantially, many still see job hopping as one of the best means of career advancement and salary increases. Companies that do not set a competitive salary range for the associated skill level, experience, and responsibilities are less likely to attract the right talent, or possibly lose candidates during negotiation.
Employees also generally expect a 13th-month bonus. While this is not mandatory, it is a widespread market norm, and one that many high-skilled candidates will expect. This bonus should therefore also be factored into the overall compensation budget from the outset, rather than treated as a discretionary add-on.
Counteroffers and negotiation are also the norm during the hiring process. With salary increases of 10 to 20 percent or more a common expectation when switching jobs, companies without a clear internal pay strategy risk inconsistent outcomes deal by deal.
Setting the wrong compensation package can have ramifications beyond a single hire. Underpricing a role can mean a longer vacancy, losing a preferred candidate, or issues with employee retention. Meanwhile, overpaying without a benchmark can erode cost control across the wider workforce.
When setting a salary range, it is also crucial to factor in the range of mandatory employer contributions that must be added to the cost, as well as additional forms of compensation that are expected. As employer social insurance and housing fund contributions add around an additional 30 to 37 percent on top of an employee’s gross salary, overestimating the salary can be costly and can translate into a meaningful budget miscalculation once applied across a workforce.
Average salaries vary considerably by region. Eastern China, which covers Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Shandong, Guangdong, and Hainan, has the highest average private-sector urban salaries in the country, at RMB 80,149 (US$11,151) in 2025, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) . That is over 30 percent higher than in the Northeastern region, the lowest-paying area on average.
Salaries vary considerably between different cities. The most expensive places to hire are tier-one cities such as Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen, while tier-two cities remain more affordable. Data from the 2025 Human Resources White Paper from the 51job HR Research Center shows that a director-level role in Shanghai paid a monthly average of RMB 36,000 (US$5,323) compared to RMB 26,183 (US$3,896) in Nanjing.
Salaries also vary greatly by industry. In general, finance and tech are the two highest-paying sectors in China. When looking at the overall economy, the average annual salary in finance in 2025 was RMB 140,451 (US$20,769), almost double the national average, while in the telecom, IT, and software industry, it was RMB 128,166 (US$18,952).
The lowest average salary was in agriculture, standing at RMB 46,552 (US$6,884).
At above-scale companies (those with an annual income of over RMB 20 million/US$3 million), IT was by far the best-paid sector, with salaries averaging RMB 242,000 (US$35,785) in 2025, and mid-level managers and above earning as much as RMB 472,000 (US$69,796).
High-skilled and technical roles in the IT industry are some of the highest paying in the country. According to data from 51job HR Research Center’s 2025 Human Resources White Paper , Cloud architects earned an average of RMB 491,253 (US$68,347) in first-tier cities in 2025 – nearly seven times the national average salary – with IC design engineers and algorithm engineers at similar levels. These are considerably higher than average benchmarks.
Foreign companies pay on average higher salaries than their domestic counterparts. According to the NBS, the average salary at large foreign-invested enterprises (FIE) exceeded RMB 160,000 (US$22,355) in 2025, compared to just under RMB 100,000 (US$13,911) at domestic private companies.
The gap widens the more senior the role is: salaries for mid-to-senior management in FIEs were more than double those paid in a domestic company.
This discrepancy is partly due to the large number of foreigners that FIEs employ. Foreign workers in China are often paid higher wages than domestic employees due to different salary expectations, especially for employees recruited from overseas, as well as minimum salary requirements for certain types of work visas , which can sometimes be many times that of local averages.
High-skilled talent in China already commands a premium. As shown above, cloud architects, IC design engineers, and algorithm engineers can earn several times the national average, even in non-first-tier citie

articles.title_orig: Stocks, Nasdaq Futures Climb as AI Trade Rebounds: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Stocks, Nasdaq Futures Climb as AI Trade Rebounds: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
Global stocks rallied on Thursday, staging a tentative recovery from an intense AI-driven sell-off and looked past a fresh set of tariffs unveiled by the White House on Wednesday.
U.S. markets will be closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday and will have a shortened trading session on Friday. During Wednesday's regular session, the Dow gained 0.33%, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% and the S&P 500 shed 0.25%, with the major averages paring losses seen earlier in the trading day.
In Europe on Thursday, equities rose sharply. The pan-European Stoxx 600 was 1.6% higher by 12:20 p.m. in London (7:20 a.m. ET), with all sectors and major bourses in positive territory.
Germany's DAX led gains on a rise of 1.9%, while the Stoxx 600 Technology index jumped 2.5%. The regional tech index has lost around 12% so far this month, amid jitters around a potential AI bubble bursting and the ousting — and return — of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO.
German semiconductor firm Infineon was more than 4% higher in afternoon trading, as chip stocks notched a boost. ASMI and ASML each gained just over 3%, while Be Semiconductor added 3.5%.
Asia-Pacific markets also rose on Thursday, with regional tech stocks also rebounded sharply, led by Japanese chip-related companies.
South Korea's Kospi gained 0.29% to close at 4,711.21, while the small-cap Kosdaq index advanced 0.78% to 655.71 after the country's central bank hiked benchmark lending rates to a 2-year high in its final meeting of the year.
Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.86% to 57,499.16 while the Topix edged 0.11% higher to 3,750.4. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.82% to 8,763.8.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was up 1.52% in its last hour of trade, while mainland China's CSI 300 edged higher marginally, closing at 3,900.55.
SoftBank Group surged more than 7%, while chip-testing equipment maker Advantest rose 4.57%. Lasertec and Disco gained , while Tokyo Electron climbed 0.59%
In South Korea, memory chip giants SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics advanced more than 2% and 0.35%, respectively. The gains followed a bruising session Wednesday amid renewed concerns over the sustainability of artificial intelligence spending.
Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, labeled it a "solid day" for regional markets, suggesting investors were hunting for opportunities in the wake of an intense global sell-off.
"The rollercoaster stock market is back on an upwards path as a new round of Trump tariffs aren't as bad as feared and the US takes the day off to celebrate Thanksgiving," he said in a note on Thursday morning. "It was notable that investors cast their net wide for opportunities, fishing for bargains in the rubble following the tech sell-off and looking at other sectors in the quest for diversification."
But Mould warned investors not to be "too complacent."
"Oil prices heading higher is not good for efforts to tame inflation, neither is the prospect of retaliation by countries on the receiving end of new US tariffs," he said.
The Trump administration on Wednesday unveiled a fresh barrage of tariffs on more than a dozen trading partners, including China, the European Union and India.
Daniela Hathorn, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said in a Thursday note that the mood in markets was "cautious rather than uniformly negative."
"European markets are attempting to rebound after yesterday's decline, while U.S. cash markets are closed for Thanksgiving, limiting the chance to test whether Wall Street's late recovery can hold," she said. "The main focus now will be trying to determine how many further increases the Fed considers necessary in early 2027 and whether AI shares can withstand that rate path while investors continue to question the returns on heavy spending."
U.S. inflation data on Wednesday reinforced expectations of further monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve. The personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.8% year on year in October, accelerating from 3.7% in September, while core inflation came in slightly above expectations at 3.3%.
Mark Haefele, chief investment officer at UBS Global Wealth Management, said in a note on Thursday morning that his team believes investors should maintain strategic allocations to equities.
But he advised market participants to "review current allocations and use market moves as an opportunity to rebalance, refocus, and strengthen portfolio resilience."

articles.title_orig: Hamas weighs response after Israel kills 10 people in Gaza
articles.title_zh: Hamas weighs response after Israel kills 10 people in Gaza
articles.content_orig:
Israel has intensified its campaign of targeted assassinations in Gaza, striking and killing Hamas commanders and political leaders, as the Trump administration urges Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to proceed with the US-brokered ceasefire plan.
On Thursday, the Israeli military killed Khaled Abu Nada, a senior member of Hamas’ Political Bureau and the organization’s Deputy Minister of Education, in a strike in central Gaza. According to a statement from Hamas, the strike on his residential apartment also killed his wife.
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said the killing of Abu Nada would disrupt Hamas’ “financial operations and its ability to formulate economic policy.” Hamas said the attack was the result of Israel’s “policy of systematic assassinations” and warned that “targeting civilian homes constitutes a continuous breach of the ceasefire agreement in Gaza and a flagrant violation of all international and humanitarian laws, norms, and conventions.”
Israeli bombardment has left Gaza a ‘toxic wasteland’ for decades to come, report says
Since the nominal ceasefire was signed more than a year ago, Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza to target Hamas. According to the Palestinian Ministry of Health, more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza in Israeli strikes or military operations over that period.
In recent weeks, Israel has escalated those strikes. On Wednesday, Israel struck and killed Muhammad Abu al-Aouf, the head of Hamas’ internal security apparatus in northern Gaza. A day earlier, the IDF killed al-Aouf’s commander, Naeem Muhammad Abu Nahal, who led Hamas’ internal security across Gaza. In each of these cases, the IDF said the assassination was a “blow” to Hamas’ leadership capabilities, even as the militant organization has firmly entrenched its power in the half of Gaza not occupied by the Israeli military.
The previous week, the IDF carried out strikes nearly every day targeting Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad, from platoon leaders to commanders of Nukhba, a special force within Hamas’ military wing.
In each case, the IDF issued virtually the same justification: “Throughout the war, and particularly recently, the terrorists advanced attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians and operated to restore the capabilities of terrorist organizations in the Gaza Strip, in systematic violation of the ceasefire.”
Hamas blamed both Israel and the US-backed Board of Peace for the ongoing attacks. The group said the board “bears political and moral responsibility for the continuation of these crimes as a result of its silence and failure to halt the aggression, and its continued provision of cover and support to the occupation.”
The board was established by the Trump administration and backed by a UN Security Council resolution to advance the Gaza ceasefire plan signed in October 2025. But the plan stalled within weeks of its implementation, and much of Gaza remains in ruins.
On Tuesday, Netanyahu spoke by phone with Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, who played a crucial role in crafting the ceasefire deal, according to an Israeli source who said they discussed Gaza.
According to Axios , Kushner urged Netanyahu to carry out Israel’s obligations under the ceasefire plan, which would require Israel to stop striking Gaza and begin withdrawing forces that occupy more than half of the enclave’s territory.
But Netanyahu has refused to make progress on the 20-point plan until Hamas is completely disarmed. Last week, Defense Minister Israel Katz said that Israel “will not withdraw from the current lines of the security zones” until Hamas is “dismantled.” He also warned that Israel is ready to occupy more of Gaza.
Hamas has refused to unilaterally disarm, saying that it would only do so alongside a staged Israeli withdrawal from Gaza
Trump’s Board of Peace chides Israel for ‘insufficient’ response to Gaza flooding
In an extensive interview with New York magazine , Kushner warned that Israel was increasingly becoming globally isolated. “I feel like the fork in the road is Israel could rise from the tragedy of October 7, (and) be much more secure and much more integrated in the world, or they can go on the current trajectory, which is to trend toward global pariah status,” he said.(and) be much more secure and much more integrated in the world, or they can go on the current trajectory, which is to trend toward global pariah status,” he said.
In another interview, with Mathias Döpfner , CEO of POLITICO’s parent company Axel Springer, Kushner called Netanyahu someone who “doesn’t always make it easy” to make progress in the Trump administration’s Gaza plan, and delivered his sharpest rebuke of Israel’s broader posture, arguing it should drop its “constant wartime mindset” and embrace economic diplomacy like Gulf Arab states do.
But Netanyahu has not shown any willingness to make concessions toward Gaza to advance the ceasefire agreement, particularly as his far-right allies have advocated for more strikes in Gaza and Palestinian emigration from the shattered territory.
On Wednesday, Kushner said in a podcast interview that Israel “needs to get out of the constant wartime mindset and focus on economic diplomacy.”
CNN’s Tal Shalev contributed to this article.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia chip buyers told to rule out Chinese renters to buy GPUs, sources say
articles.title_zh: Nvidia chip buyers told to rule out Chinese renters to buy GPUs, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Neoclouds are being told they won't be able to purchase Nvidia chips if any of the computing capacity will be rented by Chinese companies, sources told CNBC.
It comes after a new rule restricting remote access to artificial-intelligence semiconductors was announced by the Trump administration on Nov. 16.
Chip sellers communicated the messaging to neoclouds after the announcement, which seeks to close an export controls loophole allowing Chinese companies to rent access to Nvidia's most advanced chips when hosted in data centers overseas, two people familiar with the situation told CNBC. The people asked not to be named when discussing private information.
The interim final rule was announced by the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, and came into effect on Nov. 19. Previously imposed export controls have effectively banned the sale of the most advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese companies and their import into China.
Prior to the new rule's announcement, Nvidia had said it would not sell its chips to customers renting more than 50% of the graphics processing units, or GPUs, to Chinese companies, CNBC reported.
The new rule impacts the full supply chain, from the companies selling Nvidia chips to the neoclouds who rent access to computing power. Neocloud stocks have come under renewed pressure lately as investors questioned the sustainability of the AI boom.
Nvidia and the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The change has prompted Nvidia chip sellers to look for new buyers of the semiconductor giant's GPUs, CNBC reported on Wednesday, citing three people familiar with the matter. Two of those people said it appeared chip sellers were seeking to offload GPUs because they were originally for use in data centers through which Chinese companies would rent access.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that the new BIS rule was intended to close "loopholes."
"Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries," he said.
U.S. lawmakers have been looking to clamp down on China's access to advanced compute.
Separately, Nvidia warned its customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act — which has passed the House of Representatives but is yet to pass the Senate — would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing both parties to "legal action," sources previously told CNBC.

articles.title_orig: China and Brazil Lead Pushback Against Trump’s ‘Unacceptable’ Tariff Threats
articles.title_zh: China and Brazil Lead Pushback Against Trump’s ‘Unacceptable’ Tariff Threats
articles.content_orig:
U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks on reciprocal tariffs during an event at the White House on April 2, 2025.
China warned Thursday that it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” to retaliate against the Trump Administration’s proposed new tariffs , which have reignited global trade tensions.
“China urges the U.S. to correct its wrong practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation,” said He Yadong, spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce. He added that Beijing “reserves the right to take necessary measures and will resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.”
The Trump Administration targeted 14 trading partners Wednesday in a slew of new tariffs that are set to come into effect early next year. The levies will be imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 following an investigation led by U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. The U.S. said the probe had found demonstrations of unfair trade practices and excess manufacturing capacity. Mexico and Norway were not listed in the new proposals, as investigations into their respective trade practices are ongoing. Greer framed the tariffs as a way to “level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy.” The Section 301 avenue is a way for the Trump Administration to reinstate many of the tariffs that were deemed illegal and struck down by the Supreme Court in February.
China is facing a 20% tariff, which the Trump Administration said it could double to 40% if Beijing does not adhere to the terms of an existing trade truce with Washington.
Another major U.S. trading partner, Vietnam, is facing tariffs of up to 35%. The country’s Ministry of Industry and Trade said it was in the process of “developing and submitting counter-arguments to the preliminary conclusions and inaccurate opinions and allegations from relevant parties.”
The proposed tariffs are subject to a public notice and comment period, with a hearing set to take place early next year before they go into effect, allowing countries to issue responses and arguments.
Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Singapore-based Hinrich Foundation, says the proposed measures are already generating significant “resentment” among trading partners.
On top of that, the proposed rates have prompted uncertainty for major economies as to what Washington could do next. “If the U.S. unilaterally determines that the partner is not living up to expectations, then the number can ramp up higher,” she says. “That doesn't really support trust, and it makes it very hard to plan ahead.”
Amid rising tensions, several trading partners are already following China’s lead in voicing their disapproval over the rates.
Bernd Lange, trade committee chair in the European Parliament, said it was “absurd” the E.U. is facing a 20% tariff. He expressed hope that any enforced tariffs will adhere to the Turnberry agreement signed between Washington and the E.U. last year, which capped U.S. tariffs at 15%.
“Washington’s allegations about E.U. industrial overcapacity are absurd. We’ll now see whether the announced U.S. tariffs comply with Turnberry in practice,” he said. “If Washington breaches its commitments, the E.U. must act swiftly. It has the legal means to do so.”
Elms says the threat to hike rates against economies that already have a trade pact with the U.S. further calls into question “how durable” trade commitments with Washington are.
Singapore and Japan also hit back at the prospect of respective 20% tariff rates.
Singapore’s Ministry of Energy, Trade, and Industry said it was “very disappointed” by the assessment and argued that the U.S. Trade Representative’s findings “do not take into account the structure of Singapore’s economy.” Japan’s Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara referred to the U.S. tariffs as “regrettable,” insisting that: “Japan does not have any nonmarket policies or practices, or structural excess production capacity in the first place.”
Alongside the sweeping tariffs against 14 trading partners, the Trump Administration published a separate proposal seeking to raise levies on Brazil by specifically targeting its sugar and aircraft exports.
“Imposing an additional, specific tariff on sugar imports from Brazil and an additional 10% tariff on finished aircraft exports from Brazil is intended to help bring Brazil to the table,” said the office of the USTR (U.S. Trade Representative). The announcement came amid stalled trade talks between Washington and Brazil.
The Brazilian government expressed “outrage” over the proposed raising of rates, arguing that it has “been acting in good faith in negotiations” relating to Section 301 with the U.S. for over a year.
“The USTR's unilateral decision constitutes an unacceptable action within the ongoing bilateral negotiation process. Brazil will not yield to this type of threat,” the government vowed in a statement.
It said Brazil would continue to negotiate with the U.S., “without ruling out the possibility of adopting retaliatory measures in response to the illegal and unjust imposition of tariffs on Brazilian products.”
The Trump Administration could face significant pushback from the U.S. Congress next year, as Democrats will take control of both the House and Senate in January following sweeping victories in the midterms.
Senator Ron Wyden of Oregon, who will chair the Senate Finance Committee next year, has vowed to try and overturn Trump’s tariffs.
“This is another blatant attempt by Donald Trump to reconstruct his illegal global tariffs, no matter the cost to American families, workers, and small businesses. Global overcapacity is a serious problem, but Trump’s unilateral price-hiking tariffs are not the solution,” Wyden said in a statement . “As incoming Finance Committee Chairman, I will use every tool at my disposal to end Trump’s tariff chaos and restore Congress’ constitutional authority over trade.”
However, securing a veto-proof majority to rein in Trump’s authority could well prove difficult.
Among the general public, tariffs remain deeply unpopular with Americans. An NBC News exit poll following the midterm elections found that 66% of voters believed Trump’s tariff policies had hurt the national economy.

articles.title_orig: ‘War Is Hell’: A Foreign Soldier Writes Home From Ukraine
articles.title_zh: ‘War Is Hell’: A Foreign Soldier Writes Home From Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
Russia is recruiting citizens of Indonesia and the Philippines into its armed forces under the guise of civilian employment, with some foreign workers being sent to fight against Ukraine after arriving in Russia, according to a Bloomberg on November 24.
Moscow has intensified its recruitment efforts across Southeast Asia amid a shortage of military personnel for its war against Ukraine, targeting men seeking employment abroad, particularly those facing financial difficulties.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Prospective recruits are promised one-time payments of up to $35,000 upon signing military contracts, as well as monthly earnings of up to $3,000.
Recruiters advertise lucrative civilian employment opportunities in logistics, security, construction, and administration through social media. Some men arrive in Russia believing they have secured jobs in the hospitality industry or other civilian sectors, only to learn that they have unknowingly signed military service contracts.
Bloomberg noted that recruitment agents, human trafficking networks, and fraudulent recruitment operations are exploiting the vulnerability of migrant workers seeking economic opportunities abroad.
The recruitment practices have prompted authorities in both Indonesia and the Philippines to take measures aimed at protecting their citizens.
Indonesian police are investigating suspected recruitment cases as potential human trafficking offenses where there is evidence of deception or coercion into military service.
Jakarta has also urged Moscow to add Indonesia to its list of countries whose nationals are excluded from Russian military recruitment. Whether Russia has responded to the appeal remains unknown.
Meanwhile, the Philippines has stepped up efforts to combat fraudulent overseas employment schemes. With the assistance of Philippine authorities, up to 250,000 social media posts linked to such job offers have been removed.
According to Bloomberg, citing Ukrainian military figures, Russia recruited 128 Philippine nationals during the first nine months of 2026 alone.
The recruitment of foreign nationals comes amid emerging evidence of the scale of losses among foreigners serving in the Russian military.
A joint investigation by NEST Centre and Dossier Centre has identified 6,947 death records of foreign nationals believed to have been killed while fighting for Russia during its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The investigation draws on a hacked database from Russia’s state statistics agency, Rosstat, containing approximately 11.6 million death records registered between 2021 and September 2026, with Central Asian nationals accounting for the majority of the identified cases—4,091 deaths, or 58.9% of the total sample.

articles.title_orig: 75% of Rockstar’s workers have voted against unionizing
articles.title_zh: 75% of Rockstar’s workers have voted against unionizing
articles.content_orig:
UK-based Rockstar workers have voted against unionizing.
The IWGB, a union representing some Rockstar workers, has confirmed that workers rejected a deal that would recognize the Rockstar Game Workers Union.
The two-week ballot, which ran from 12 to 26 November, overlapped with the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 . The results were roughly 25% in favor of recognizing the union, and 75% against, with the vast majority of its around 1,600 employees participating.
Recognition would have established a formal framework for workers to negotiate collectively over pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, pensions, and the impact of AI and redundancies.
The result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives. The union is also able to continue representing individual members.
The IWGB says that this has not dissuaded them, and they will continue to try and “win the trust” of Rockstar employees.
“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for,” a statement from the IWGB reads.
“Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.
“Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening,” the statement continues. “We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions will lead us.
“A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it’s one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against Al and layoffs.”
In its own statement, Rockstar Games said it was “extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of GTA 6.”
“This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong,” said Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing. “As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.”
This comes amid an employment tribunal into alleged union busting at Rockstar .
In 2025, Rockstar dismissed 34 workers who were active in the workplace’s union efforts. They say they were let go as part of an effort to stop these efforts, whereas Rockstar says they were dismissed for leaking confidential information .

articles.title_orig: Big Apple retail blues: More than 16,000 NYC storefronts sit empty as businesses struggle
articles.title_zh: Big Apple retail blues: More than 16,000 NYC storefronts sit empty as businesses struggle
articles.content_orig:
As more shoppers ditch their local mom-and-pop for online stores, New York City storefronts are reaching shocking vacancy levels.
Over 16,000 storefronts across the five boroughs are sitting empty as business closings have outpaced openings for three straight years, according to fresh data from city Comptroller Mark Levine’s office.
The city’s storefront vacancy rate climbed to 11.32% in the third quarter of 2026 from 11.26% in the previous three-month period — with Brooklyn and Queens faring worse than they did in late 2023.
The report “is another wake-up call,” Andrew Rigie, executive director of the NYC Hospitality Alliance, told The Post. “The city must focus not only on helping new businesses open, but also on keeping existing ones from shuttering.”
Some 2,551 storefront businesses closed between July and September, while just 2,275 opened, resulting in a net loss of 276, according to the comptroller’s newly launched Storefront Vacancy Dashboard.
Small businesses accounted for nearly three-quarters of the net losses, with 2,201 shutting down and 1,996 opening.
The number of storefront businesses opening fell 16.1% from the previous quarter, while closings declined 17.4%.
The latest figures mark the 12th consecutive quarter in which storefront closings have exceeded openings.
Meanwhile, more than 10,000 spaces previously occupied by small businesses remain vacant.
Manhattan continues to have the highest vacancy rate among the five boroughs at 13.12% — down considerably from its post-pandemic peak of 15.8% in late 2023.
Brooklyn, however, is closing in on Manhattan with a vacancy rate of 12.68%, while Queens has registered the biggest increase of any borough since 2023, reaching 9.8%.
About one in five storefronts sits empty in parts of the Financial District, Tribeca, Ocean Hill, East New York and Old Astoria.
“Manhattan’s recovery is real, but it’s uneven, and the corridors that are still struggling tend to share a few problems,” Jessica Walker, president and CEO of the Manhattan Chamber of Commerce, told The Post.
“Blocks that lived on five-day office workers or a single anchor tenant lost their base, while neighborhoods with residents, tourists and nightlife have bounced back faster.”
The difficulties facing neighborhood merchants have persisted despite a rebound in tourism and a 6.4% increase in citywide taxable sales in fiscal 2026.
Business owners, meanwhile, have been grappling with higher expenses for everything from utilities and insurance to labor.
The city’s minimum wage rose to $17 an hour in January, while consumer prices in the New York metropolitan area climbed 4.5% in the 12 months through September.
A Federal Reserve Bank of New York survey found that service businesses in New York and northern New Jersey reported an average cost increase of about 7% in 2025.
Subsequent survey results identified employee health insurance, utilities and business insurance as particularly fast-rising expenses.
Vacancy rates were particularly steep among storefronts classified as vape and cigar shops, at roughly 26%, and furniture and home goods retailers, at nearly 16%, according to the comptroller.
Roughly 13.5% of clothing storefronts are vacant, as are more than 10% of spaces previously occupied by bars.
In some neighborhoods, the problem isn’t merely that businesses are folding — it’s that finding new tenants can take years.
A separate report released by Levine’s office in June found that in parts of Williamsburg, Crown Heights, Astoria, Midtown and the Upper East and Upper West sides, more than 60% of vacant small-business storefronts had been empty for at least two years.
Walker said some of the hardest-to-fill spaces were once occupied by pharmacies, banks and chain retailers.
“Those spaces are far larger than what a local restaurant, salon or shop can use, and dividing them up is expensive and slow,” she told The Post.
Even when landlords find tenants, regulatory hurdles can keep businesses from opening their doors for months, Walker added.
“Between building permits, inspections, liquor licensing and community board review, a new tenant can wait many months, often more than a year, paying rent before making a dollar,” she said.
Walker also pointed to longstanding scaffolding, major construction projects and Manhattan’s Commercial Rent Tax as deterrents.
“That’s why so many spaces stay empty for years, not months.”
The report also found little evidence that corporate chains were systematically displacing mom-and-pop merchants.
Of the roughly 96,500 storefronts occupied by small businesses at the outset of 2020, just 2,150 had been taken over by chains.
The Mamdani administration has announced more than 50 reforms aimed at helping small businesses, including efforts to streamline permitting and licensing and address the costs of rent, insurance and utilities.
Ashley Ranslow, New York state director of the National Federation of Independent Business, pinned the blame on the City Council’s regulatory agenda.
“From paid and unpaid leave requirements to the threat of new lawsuits, it’s becoming nearly impossible for a small business owner to operate in New York City,” Ranslow told The Post.
Walker called for firm deadlines for permit approvals, opportunities for merchants to correct violations before being fined and relief from the Commercial Rent Tax.
She also urged the city to help landlords subdivide larger vacant storefronts and provide incentives for long-term leases with independent businesses.
The comptroller’s office plans to update its storefront dashboard every quarter, tracking openings, closings and vacancies down to the neighborhood level.
“With 15,000 restaurant and bar jobs lost over the past year, high labor costs, insurance premiums, rents, inflation, costly litigation, and bureaucratic red tape are squeezing small businesses,” Rigie said.
“Our elected leaders must focus on reducing the costs and burdens of doing business here, not adding to them, if we want to fill empty storefronts and keep New Yorkers employed.”

articles.title_orig: Apple pulls Chinese-developed AI chatbot from App Store over reports of sexual messages to kids
articles.title_zh: Apple pulls Chinese-developed AI chatbot from App Store over reports of sexual messages to kids
articles.content_orig:
People walk past the Minimax booth during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai, China, July 17, 2026. ( Reuters/Go Nakamura/File )
Apple has yanked an AI chatbot app with roughly 11 million monthly users from its App Store worldwide after reports alleged the platform’s virtual characters sent sexually inappropriate messages to children .
The app, Talkie, is developed by Shanghai-based MiniMax and was removed this week following Wednesday reports by Australia's ABC News and the United Kingdom's Bureau of Investigative Journalism that its AI-generated characters sent abusive messages to minors.
Although Talkie carries an 18+ rating on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store and states that children aged under 14 or under 16 cannot sign up, depending on the country, child safety advocates have criticized its lax verification safeguards that allow users to self-report their age.
INSTAGRAM'S AI MAY CATCH TEENS LYING ABOUT THEIR AGE
MiniMax founder and CEO Yan Junjie, second from left, and COO Yun Yeyim, second from right, pose with Hong Kong Stock Exchange CEO Bonnie Chan, far left, and Chairman Carlson Tong at the Chinese artificial intelligence model developer's listing cerem (Reuters/Kane Wu / Reuters Photos)
Apple told FOX Business that the company enforces strict App Review Guidelines prohibiting offensive, sexual or pornographic material and previously took action against the platform.
Apple originally rejected Talkie: Personalized AI Chats in July 2023 for carrying a 13+ rating, requiring the developer to raise it to 18+ before launch. Apple later removed that app in December 2024 over objectionable user-generated content and subsequently pulled the developer's other app, Talkie Lab - AI Playground, for sexual content.
Apple also noted that as of Nov. 16, developers can declare whether their apps include "Dating and Relationships" features — which automatically triggers a minimum 18+ rating — with all apps required to complete those disclosures by Jan. 12, 2027. In Australia, Apple users must confirm they are 18 or older before downloading 18+-rated apps.
FOX Business has reached out to MiniMax for comment.
Launched in 2023, Talkie promotes itself with the tagline "Your dream chat partner awaits" and offers companions designed for sustained emotional engagement and human-like interactions, often with romantic undertones and immersive storylines.
Tama Leaver, an internet studies professor at Curtin University, told ABC News the platform's approach is particularly risky for young people still learning to navigate relationships.
"These tools really push on the edges of trying to keep young people engaging as much as possible, but there is no real sense of appropriateness in doing so," Leaver said. "It might be the case that a young person is actually investing quite heavily in the emotional landscape of… these apps and making themselves quite vulnerable."
An Apple App Store icon is displayed on a phone screen in this illustration photo taken in Krakow, Poland, on Jan. 29, 2023. (Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images / Getty Images)
Together with its Chinese version, Xingye, Talkie generated over 60% of MiniMax's income in 2024 before the company stopped breaking out chatbot-related revenue shares this year.
AI IS CHANGING MODERN DATING, BUT EXPERTS WARN IT'S MAKING PEOPLE 'RELATIONALLY STUPID'
Other AI platforms have faced similar backlash over child safety this year. Elon Musk's Grok AI chatbot drew criticism from governments after it was used to create sexualized images of women and children , and AI companion maker Character.ai faces several U.S. lawsuits over its chatbots' inappropriate interactions with minors.
GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO BY CLICKING HERE
In July, China cracked down on domestic AI companion apps, including Xingye, banning intimate relationships for minors and ordering platforms to develop strict guardrails to curb emotional dependency and addiction risks.
Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Norse Atlantic suspends all flights as it faces potential collapse
articles.title_zh: Norse Atlantic suspends all flights as it faces potential collapse
articles.content_orig:
The Norwegian low cost carrier Norse Atlantic Airways has suspended all flights as it rushes to resolve what it warned is a critical financial situation.
The airline said if no solution can be found, it intends to file for bankruptcy.
The airline uses a fleet of 12 Boeing 787 aircraft on long-haul routes from a number of European airports, including London Gatwick, Rome and Oslo.
Prior to the suspension of flights, it was advertising services from London to Orlando, Cape Town, Bangkok and Phuket.
One aircraft was meant to depart London for Orlando this morning, while another was meant to arrive from Cape Town this evening.
The suspension has also affected Pakistan International Airlines, which had been leasing aircraft and crews from Norse Atlantic.
PIA was forced to cancel services from London to Islamabad and from Manchester to Lahore last night.
In a statement on social media, PIA said all UK flights from today would be operated by aircraft from its own fleet.
Londoner Fred was due to fly to Cape Town with Norse Atlantic next week for a friend's wedding, but has decided to change his plans.
"Yesterday the exact same flight I was going to get was cancelled, so I was worried" he told the BBC's Your Voice. "I sent an email to Norse and have had nothing back".
He decided to rebook with a different airline, which cost him an extra £1,000.
Another traveller, Claire from Herefordshire, is currently on holiday in South Africa with her daughter.
"We are due to fly home on Sunday and are now looking at a really expensive flight back," she said.
"We have tried contacting Norse but have been given an automated response saying someone will get back to us within three business days."
Consumer group Which? advised Norse Atlantic customers to not cancel their flights as the airline has not collapsed. Doing so removes passengers' right to a refund.
Rory Boland, Which? travel editor, said: "If Norse does go bust, whether you get a refund depends on how you booked and paid. If you booked directly with Norse, you may be able to claim a refund via your credit card provider, or possibly your debit card."
Those stuck abroad should contact insurers, while those with package holidays reliant on Norse Atlantic flights should contact their tour operator, he added.
Norse Atlantic Airways was set up in 2021 as a low-cost long-haul carrier.
It entered the market as a successor to Norwegian, which withdrew from long haul routes as a result of the Covid pandemic.
But it has struggled to make money, and its problems worsened this year, as fuel prices rocketed due to the war in Iran.
Unlike many other European carriers, Norse Atlantic does not hedge its fuel bills by buying supplies in advance at fixed prices.
This left it fully exposed when prices soared, with the cost of fuel roughly doubling at one point. Prices remain significantly higher than they were before the conflict began.
In the first half of the year Norse Atlantic made a loss of $94.6m.
In a statement to the Oslo Stock Exchange on Wednesday, the airline said its financial situation was critical, and it needed to find short term funding to continue its operations.
After suspending flights, the company said it was in discussions with investors regarding a possible takeover that "would include a financing solution".
However, it said if short term funding could not be found quickly, "it is the Board's intention to file for bankruptcy".
Norse Atlantic had been looking for a buyer since July.
Its potential collapse follows the failure of Spirit Airlines in May . The US-based low cost carrier was another airline left exposed when jet fuel prices soared, as US airlines typically do not hedge their purchases.
If Norse Atlantic were to fold, it would be another major setback for the low-cost long-haul model, which has typically proved popular with passengers but difficult to sustain financially, especially on transatlantic routes.
Additional reporting by Rozina Sini

articles.title_orig: Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos set to lead European Central Bank
articles.title_zh: Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos set to lead European Central Bank
articles.content_orig:
Pablo Hernández de Cos is set to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank next year.
He received backing from euro zone leaders at the European Council Summit, multiple media reported on Thursday.
The role still requires formal appointment after consultation with the European Parliament and the ECB's Governing Council, but neither has veto power and the decision follows intense political wrangling to reach a consensus on who should serve the eight-year term.
Reuters reported that de Cos was set for the nomination after the Netherlands agreed to back Klaas Knot, the only other candidate, citing European diplomatic sources.
De Cos is a 55-year-old economist and career central banker who rose through the ranks of the Bank of Spain, starting as a researcher in the 1990s and working in various departments before becoming governor from 2018 to June 2024.
He chaired the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision from 2019 to 2024, and has been General Manager of the Basel-based Bank for International Settlements since July 2025.
Both de Cos and his main rival for the ECB top job, Knot, were widely seen as candidates with deep knowledge and experience in monetary policy and financial stability — attributes that took on particular importance at a time of resurgent inflation, fragmentation and political uncertainty.
Lagarde had extensive experience in financial institutions but was criticized by some early in her tenure for a lack of central banking experience.
De Cos gained sufficient political backing in closed-door discussions and negotiations since Lagarde said she would step down on Feb. 7, 2027, over seven years after she became the first woman to helm the ECB. That was despite a final push by the Netherlands at the European Council meeting this week backing Knot.
Representatives from the euro area's biggest economies — Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands — have been horse-trading as they look to secure representation on the central bank's six-member Executive Board.
Influential roles as chief economist, expected to go to Germany's Markus Brunnermeier, and head of the Markets Portfolio, for which France's Laurence Boone has reportedly been tapped, also change hands in 2027.
Analysts say de Cos's commentary and actions over more than two decades at Spain's central bank paint him as moderately dovish — inclined to favor lower interest rates to support economic growth — but also as a pragmatist who has been willing to adapt.
That has included support for strong rate hikes during the energy price shock that followed Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, but also giving staunch backing for rates below zero and the huge stimulus package launched by then-ECB President Mario Draghi to reboot the euro zone economy in 2019.
De Cos quipped in 2024 that he was an "owl" after being asked if he was a hawk or a dove, emphasizing his focus on data and the situation at hand.
"It is true that Hernández de Cos supported the ECB's uber-dovish monetary policy during the period when inflation was persistently below target. However, his monetary policy views may well be regime-dependent," Christian Kopf, head of fixed income and foreign exchange at Union Investment, said in emailed comments.
"We are now clearly in a higher-inflation regime, with core inflation in the euro area expected to remain above the ECB's target through 2029."
Kopf added that de Cos was the candidate with the "strongest technical understanding of monetary policy and central banking," which he said was important at a time when the world is "witnessing an assault on central bank independence, not only in the United States but also in countries such as Japan."
"By appointing a career technocrat such as Hernández de Cos as ECB President, the European Council would send a strong signal that Europe will not waver in its commitment to price stability and that the euro will remain a hard currency," Kopf said.
Spain's de Cos as president, Germany's Brunnermeier as chief economist and France's Boone as head of market operations represent a "carefully crafted package deal," Kopf also noted, because it balances representation from northern and southern European countries. The result was partially due to the knock-on effects of the German government pushing hard for the chief economist position, he said.
Along with a desire among politicians for influence, a north-south balance is seen as important as the northern countries are seen as leaning more hawkish — more inclined to opt for rate hikes and restrictive policy to tame inflation — while southern are perceived as more dovish.
John Orchard, chairman of the Digital Monetary Institute at think tank OMFIF, said that as a "central banker's central banker," de Cos had "managed to earn respect from typically hawkish northern observers."
Another supportive factor of de Cos's candidacy was the stellar growth rate of many of those southern economies in recent years.
Once the "sick men" of the euro area's 2010s sovereign debt crisis, Portugal, Italy , Spain and Greece have become some of the bloc's strongest growth drivers in recent years .
Factors such as strong tourism, relative political stability, increased foreign investment and strengthening public finances have boosted southern economies. Meanwhile, the euro zone's traditional powerhouse Germany has stuttered amid soaring industrial costs and a struggling autos market .
Orchard said that some believed that Lagarde's presidency had ushered in an "esprit de corps" at the ECB, with policymakers focused on the interests of the whole European economy.
That would, in theory, reduce the importance of nationality among leadership and of traditional notions of hawkish northern nations and dovish southern ones. However, Orchard also noted the recurrent theme of national representation in the recent debate and the perception of Knot as a hawkish choice.
Diverging performance is a core challenge for any leader of the ECB, which must set monetary policy for 21 economies all growing at different speeds and with their own domestic priorities and inflationary pressures.
But it has become particularly pressing this year as the bloc's second-biggest economy, France, is teetering on the edge of its own potential debt crisis .
Moves in French markets and whether the ECB needs to take more extreme measures beyond continuing to urge fiscal discipline will remain in focus for de Cos.
The ECB Executive Board's view of what measures could be taken to prevent market disorder and under what conditions was a key topic under discussion when choosing who should fill the roles, according to insiders.
Despite political efforts to pass a budget that will reduce its budget deficit to around 5% of GDP, investors have been driving up French borrowing costs on concerns over its mounting public debt-to-GDP ratio , high budget deficit and contracting economy .
Risks are being compounded by political uncertainty ahead of France's presidential election in April, which is stymying business activity and raising wider questions about EU unity as far-right and far-left candidates pull ahead.
Rising French yields and the widening spread in France's borrowing costs over Germany's have led to speculation over whether the ECB might need to deploy tools such as liquidity injections or its never-used Transmission Protection Instrument to protect other countries from contagion and support the euro.
This would be politically controversial unless France agreed to stringent fiscal discipline measures akin to those that southern nations signed up to during the Sovereign Debt Crisis — which could be complicated if far-right presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, who has a combative relationship with EU institutions, wins.

articles.title_orig: Iranian attack on Kuwait kills two Italians, Italy’s foreign minister says
articles.title_zh: Iranian attack on Kuwait kills two Italians, Italy’s foreign minister says
articles.content_orig:
Two Italian nationals have died after an Iranian strike on a facility in Kuwait, Italy's foreign ministry has said.
The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, the ministry added.
Kuwait's defence ministry earlier said that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.
Iran has denied responsibility, with armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi saying "no military or offensive operations have been conducted" by its military.
It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country.
Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.
The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.
Kuwait's Army said the latest attack was on a "vital site in the country" and was the result of "heinous Iranian aggression", while confirming the deaths of the two Italian nationals.
Meanwhile, Italy's foreign ministry said in a statement: "An explosion caused by a drone attack... occurred at a site where two Italian technicians from the company Rheinmetall Italia were working."
The two Italian nationals were working at an air defence detection station and performing maintenance work on systems used by the Kuwaiti Armed Forces, according to Italian press agency Ansa, citing Italy's foreign ministry.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on X: "On my own behalf and on behalf of the government, I express my deepest sympathy and offer my heartfelt condolences to the victims' families.
"My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families."
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on social media: "We must step up pressure on Iran to end these unacceptable attacks against its neighbours and our partners in the Gulf.
"Today's events are a further reminder that security in the Gulf is a security issue for us all."

articles.title_orig: Med Emre: Diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes sinks near Ibiza, killing one
articles.title_zh: Med Emre: Diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes sinks near Ibiza, killing one
articles.content_orig:
An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has capsized off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.
The Med Emre, a Malta-flagged vessel, was carrying 17 crew members who were all rescued. However seven were taken to hospital and one was later pronounced dead, Balearic Islands emergency services confirmed.
The six crew receiving treatment reportedly suffered minor injuries, such as hypothermia, Spanish media reports.
The possible environmental damage is being assessed by a plane and Spain's pollution control vessel, Clara Campoamor, which is owned by the country's national maritime rescue service.
"There is still little information available about a possible fuel spill," Balearic Islands' President Marga Prohens wrote on X.
Regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz said the tanker had not completely sunk, as had been originally reported. The vessel remains, however, partially submerged.
That made conditions more favourable for carrying out recovery operations, he said, "as we have gone from the possibility of the vessel being at a depth of 1,000m to a situation that allows operations to be carried out on the surface".
The Med Emre capsized 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia. It is unclear what caused the sinking.
The chemical tanker was en route from Algeciras, in southern Spain, to Barcelona in the north-east.
Rescuers in Valencia received a distress call around 22:30 local time (21:30 GMT) on Wednesday, according to Spanish media. Minutes later, the vessel reported a leak and the crew said it was leaning at a 90-degree angle.
The injured crew members have been taken to hospitals in Valencia and Can Misses Hospital in Ibiza, President Prohens said.
Ibiza's marine environment was added to the Unesco World Heritage List in 1999. In particular, it is home to dense prairies of Posidonia oceanic seagrass, which is found only in the Mediterranean basin and plays a vital role in supporting local marine biodiversity.
In 2002, Spain experienced one of its worst environmental disasters when the Prestige oil tanker ran into trouble off Galicia's coastline . It spilled more than 60,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil into the sea.

articles.title_orig: Net Migration to U.K. Falls to Lowest Level Since 1997, Excluding Pandemic
articles.title_zh: Net Migration to U.K. Falls to Lowest Level Since 1997, Excluding Pandemic
articles.content_orig:
Net migration to the UK has fallen to 77,000 in the year to the end of June - the lowest level this century, other than during the pandemic, Office for National Statistics (ONS) figures show.
Excluding the limited movements of people during the worldwide travel restrictions in 2020, the figures show the number of people arriving in the UK, minus those leaving, tumbled 92% from the record high of 944,000 in the year to March 2023.
The ONS said this was the lowest net migration since 1997.
Net migration is a measure of how many extra people are added  to the population in a given year.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the figures showed there was now "a sufficient degree of control" over the migration system.
The prime minister went on to say: "I'm not going to say all of the work is done, and I don't want to appear complacent, but I think we're finally as a country getting into the position that the public has long wanted to see."
The underlying official statistics show that an estimated 738,000 people immigrated to the UK in the year to June while 661,000 emigrated.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the figures showed that Labour had "delivered" after Conservative failures - but Chris Philp, her Tory shadow, said restrictions introduced by his party before the 2024 General Election were behind the falls.
The 77,000 figure is also the first time the UK has seen net migration in the tens of thousands since former PM David Cameron's controversial pledge 16 years ago to reach such a level.
The biggest factors in Thursday's record low were falls in the arrivals of people coming from outside Europe in three major categories of migration: The number of people coming to the UK to work fell by 45,000, asylum claims fell by 19,000 and the total number of students fell by 33,000.
These number had been expected to fall because of the tightening of visas rules that began under the previous Conservative government which was then continued by Labour from July 2024.
The effect of those policies, plus emigration from the UK, has meant that while net migration had already begun to fall, it more than halved in the last 12 months alone.
Mahmood said the figures showed the government had "restored control".
"We have brought net migration to 77,000, down 92% from its peak under the Conservatives," she said. "Where they failed, we have delivered for the British people."
This is a reference to the so-called "Boris Wave" after Brexit. When the UK left the EU and its freedom of movement rules, Boris Johnson's government allowed in many more people to work and study from other parts of the world.
That led to the record-breaking arrivals in the year to March 2023. Johnson's successor, Rishi Sunak, introduced major restrictions on visas in the last months of his government.
Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said the falls were a result of those changes.
In a post on X, he called for an "annual legally binding inward migration cap, set by Parliament, at far lower levels".
Dr Ben Brindle of Oxford University's Migration Observatory, an impartial expert body, said: "We are entering an unusual period where immigration has come down and may still have further to fall - but we still have relatively high emigration, at least for the time being.
"Most of those emigrants are non-citizens, including people who arrived a few years ago when immigration was very high. That could push the net migration figures down even further next year, but the downwards blip is unlikely to last forever."
In the year to June some 73,000 people arriving in the UK seeking asylum - down from 93,000 the previous year.
As of September, the number of people who were waiting for a decision was 41,000, down 49% on the previous year.
The Home Office said that these changes were driven by speeding up the system in taking decisions and a fall in the arrivals of new claimants via  "illegal entry routes" - largely meaning English Channel small boats.
As a result, the number of people accommodated in September by the Home Office was 93,000 - 16% lower than the year before. Some 52 hotels that had been dedicated to asylum seekers have been emptied this year. While some 140 are still in use the total number of people in hotels has fallen 64% to 13,000.
Responding to the latest statistics, Reform UK's home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf said the figures were "no cause for celebration".
"This population explosion is why British people struggle to get a GP appointment, can't get housing and our prisons are overwhelmed."
Liberal Democrat asylum and immigration spokesperson Paul Kohler said: "Britain faces serious demographic and economic challenges, and urgently needs a proper immigration plan to support our economy and public services."
A spokesperson for the Green Party added: "Creating a harsh environment for migrants and people seeking asylum is not a measure of success. The British people are overwhelmingly compassionate and will not be taken in by the dangerous and opportunistic narratives of the far right."

articles.title_orig: The GTA 6 Spoiler Interview Pt. 1: Rockstar on that Chapter 1 twist, cut content, and more
articles.title_zh: The GTA 6 Spoiler Interview Pt. 1: Rockstar on that Chapter 1 twist, cut content, and more
articles.content_orig:
“How on earth did you keep that a secret?”
That was one of the first questions I asked Rob Nelson , producer of Grand Theft Auto 6 and co-studio head at Rockstar North , as we sat down for a lengthy, wide-ranging conversation about the game. I got the feeling that he, and everyone else at Rockstar , was absolutely desperate to speak to someone from the outside world.
It was days before the game was due to release, and despite everything that’s happened to Rockstar during the development of its latest epic, this one, frankly giant, story detail hadn’t been spread across the internet.
Was Rockstar ever going to talk about the fact that Jason and Lucia’s motivation, the driving force behind GTA 6, was there as-yet-unheard-of, son?
“Oh my God, I’m so happy,” Nelson tells me as I recount my shock at the reveal. “No, we never were going to [reveal it]. I am still holding on. Fingers crossed, how many more days? I’m praying it stays under wraps. Given everything that we’ve gone through, every day I’m just like, ‘please, please don’t do that, please don’t do that’.”
Perhaps no game in history has been subject to more high-profile leaks and cyberattacks, so the fact that (beyond some light forum chatter that was largely dismissed at the time) there was virtually no evidence of Jason and Lucia’s son anywhere on the internet is striking.
“It’s meant to shock,” Nelson says. “We were watching everyone speculate about the nature of their relationship and Jason’s character, and that takes it in a completely different context. You have something to strive for beyond a huge bank account at the end.”
As we spoke, Grand Theft Auto 6 was in the midst of taking over the world. Every mainstream news outlet had a story on people taking days off to play it. A pop-up store in London’s Selfridges attracted five-hour queues, with virtually all merchandise flying off the shelf on the first day.
Nelson was only an hour away on the other side of the M8, but I got the sense he, and by extension the team, were somewhere else entirely. “It’s a very surreal feeling. We’re extremely nervous. It’s very nice to be able to talk to someone who’s played it. You never know; it’s very different. I hope it’s a very different and a very familiar thing.
“We were watching everyone speculate about the nature of their relationship and Jason’s character, and that takes it in a completely different context.”
“We’re very nervous about that and how people react to it. It’s been a long time since we’ve shipped any of these. For us, it’s been 2018 since Red Dead 2. Time is dragging, the days are dragging. I think with everything that we’ve gone through, I’m just sitting here hoping more stuff doesn’t get spoiled. That experience of going through it for the first time is everything.”
Nelson tells me that he’s not been able to look at, much less play the game for a while. “I can’t look at it. I have to go do something else. A couple of weeks ago I had to play it for a couple of people, and I’ve not touched it since. People ask how I deal with the pressure of the expectation.
“It’s super intense, it’s super, super intense, all the way through, but I think I was always able to sort of compartmentalize it a little bit. I liken it to when you hear about a sports team in a seven-game series – just focus on the next game. We go out there to do what we’ve got to do.”
What the development team has done is deliver what is perhaps Rockstar’s greatest game. It’s a crime story that retains the spirit of GTA while leaving some elements of the past behind. While some fans in the days since release have highlighted older features they’d have liked to see included, Nelson tells me it’s not that simple.
“You’re aware of the noise all the way through development, and you’re aware of what people want, but with GTA 6, it means so much and so many different things to so many people. You’ve got to listen, but you’ve always got to ask what is important to us.
“Is it going to end up a mush? It’s challenging enough with the game being made by this many people, but we’ve ended up with something that feels very singular in terms of its version.”
One major change to Grand Theft Auto 6 is the game’s new criminal profile system, something that players have heralded as a new element of role-playing, but it’s also garnered pushback from players who want to rampage across Vice City without repercussions.
“You’re aware of the noise all the way through development, and you’re aware of what people want, but with GTA 6, it means so much and so many different things to so many people”
Nelson says that’s exactly what he expected. “It was funny, when we first started doing press for the game, it was fun, but it was frustrating because we had to talk in very abstract terms about things. But TGG (a GTA-focussed YouTube creator) was one of the early guys we showed stuff, and when he saw the little icon come up he said ‘what is that?’ He really pressed me on it: ‘Is that morality?’ and he said he couldn’t believe we did that and that it was going to change GTA.
“I thought, ‘oh shit, we’re in trouble’ but I said ‘it doesn’t change everything, it changes what GTA can be’. So for us, I think it opens a new range of choices and decisions for the player to make. You can still do whatever you wanted to do before, but now you have other options.”
Nelson says the system was designed to be additive, but that he knows and expects some players to “reject this new stuff we’re offering.”
“I hope it changes the way players who want to engage with it play the game. In GTA 5 you started with a bank robbery in North Yankton, and you’re murdering like 40 cops off the rip, and you’re setting these guys up as what they are.
“We were conscious of that. Lucia takes the bullets out of the gun at the start of the game. She goes in, and it’s not like you can kill a bunch of people. So we wanted to start them off with a bit less baggage. They’re trying to make a go of this semi-legitimate life.
“When you pick up with Jason, he’s still a criminal; he’s still getting in trouble with Donnie and all that, but he’s sort of been living this relatively criminal-adjacent existence.”
This lack of baggage plays into one of Grand Theft Auto 6’s more noticeable changes. Hyper-violent weapons, like the chainsaw and the katana, which appeared in previous entries, are gone. “As far as the chainsaw – I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters,” Nelson tells me. “ It’s not a resource thing.”
“Even at the most psycho, did Jason and Lucia really need that – what’s that going to look like?” Chainsaws physically appear in the game, but you can’t pick them up. In a game where players are trained to interact with most of the world, I asked about how the team decides something should be decoration only.
“Lucia takes the bullets out of the gun at the start of the game. She goes in, and it’s not like you can kill a bunch of people. So we wanted to start them off with a bit less baggage”
“You’re always trying to find what is the right sort of line and the right balance, it really just depends, you want to feel like you can interact with as much as the world as possible.”
Rob cites tennis, volleyball, darts, and golf as something you can’t do fully, but they’d have loved to with unlimited time. “We want to do everything, we want to pick up every guitar, we want to sit at the drums. Did we need to do full golf?” He laughs. “It’s not really these characters’ thing.”
Nelson explained that Rockstar decided against including a parody of Disney World for similar reasons. “It’s about whether there’s a narrative reason to spend that time to make a fully functioning theme park. We just figure out what we do need to support the story and support the feeling of being in Leonida.
“A theme park would represent a lot of work that we didn’t have, and we didn’t have a strong narrative reason to send them there,” he added. “That’s the challenge: where do you stop? When

articles.title_orig: Thailand's Bangchak shuts all units at Bangkok refinery after fire, says 9 workers injured
articles.title_zh: Thailand's Bangchak shuts all units at Bangkok refinery after fire, says 9 workers injured
articles.content_orig:
An explosion and a fire at an oil facility in Bangkok has injured at least nine people, authorities said, as residents in the surrounding area were urged to evacuate their homes.
Thailand’s Bangchak Corp said on Thursday it has shut down all production units at its Phra Khanong oil refinery following a fire.
At least nine people were injured in the fire, four of those seriously, according to Bangkok’s Erawan Emergency Medical Centre.
The sprawling site in eastern Bangkok is run by Thai energy conglomerate Bangchak Corporation. Based on a preliminary investigation, the incident occurred at the refinery’s hydrocracking unit, the company said.
The company said the Pollution Control Department conducted air quality measurements within a 3-4 km radius of the refinery and confirmed that the air quality was within normal ranges.
Thailand’s Energy minister Akanat Promphan, visiting the scene, told reporters it appeared the fire broke out at a distillation tower, “which was at least 100 metres (330 feet) away from the oil depot”, limiting the damage.
Videos posted on social media showed flames rising high above the site in eastern Bangkok, and thick black smoke sweeping across the Thai capital’s skyline.
“For their own safety, members of the public in the vicinity are urged to evacuate the area immediately,” the Bangna District Office said in a statement on its Facebook page.
Al Jazeera’s Tony Cheng, reporting from Chiang Mai, said the explosion was heard at about 3pm local time (08:00 GMT). The oil facility is “fairly close to the city centre, but still in a remote area that has a lot of industrial offices, warehouses, and near to Bangkok’s main port”, he said.
“The authorities say the fire was brought under control,” Cheng said, adding that “the highway and most of the major traffic routes in that area are still operational.”
Cheng said the large plume of black smoke would have pushed the authorities to share the evacuation warning. “We have seen industrial accidents in that area in the past couple of years,” he added.
“It serves not just Bangkok, but a large part of central Thailand. Most of the oil imports coming into this part of Thailand go here,” he added. “We don’t know at this stage the full extent of the damage, but one would imagine that it is quite considerable.”
Bangchak Corporation’s website describes the site as a “modern complex refinery with a maximum capacity of 120,000 barrels per day”.
An explosion occurred at the refinery in July 2012 — owned by then Bangchak Petroleum, which became the Bangchak Corporation — triggering a massive fire but no reported injuries.
At the time, there were questions asked about why such a large facility was located in what is now a residential area of Bangkok.
